headline: Oil Nears $100 as Middle East War Strains Petrochemical Supplies
summary: Crude oil traded near $100 per barrel as the ongoing US-Iran conflict turned petrochemical gluts into shortages in Asia, pushing Chinese petrochemical inflation to 5% in September.
why: Elevated energy costs and feedstock shortages ripple through global manufacturing, lifting headline consumer inflation and central bank interest rate expectations.

impacts.name: Brent Crude
impacts.why: Prolonged military conflict in the Persian Gulf disrupts crude and petrochemical shipments, tightening international supplies.

impacts.name: China
impacts.why: Higher imported feedstock prices increase production costs and compress profit margins across industrial manufacturing.

why_moved: Crude oil maintained elevated prices near $100 per barrel due to lingering geopolitical supply risks in the Gulf, keeping global inflation risks front and center.
